arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
#
# The backup destination is environment-specific and is not baked into this
# repo. Set it via the BACKUP_DEST environment variable before running (e.g.
# in the crontab entry or the environment registered by register-job.sh):
#
#   BACKUP_DEST=/mnt/backups            (local path or mounted volume)
#   BACKUP_DEST=user@host:/path/to/dir  (remote host, copied with scp)
#
# If BACKUP_DEST is unset, the script fails loudly instead of silently
# skipping the copy step, so a missing configuration is noticed immediately
# rather than discovered when a restore is needed.
set -eu

DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "backup.sh: BACKUP_DEST is not set; refusing to run without a backup destination" >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [ ! -d logs ]; then
    echo "backup.sh: logs/ directory not found" >&2
    exit 1
fi

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Remote destination in host:path form; copy over scp.
        scp -q "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # Local path or mounted volume.
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command:
chmod +x backup.sh
sh -n backup.sh && echo "syntax OK"
mkdir -p logs && echo hi > logs/a.log
# test local dest
BACKUP_DEST=$(mktemp -d) sh backup.sh
echo exit=$?
ls "$(dirname /tmp)" >/dev/null
# test missing dest
unset BACKUP_DEST
sh backup.sh; echo exit=$?
rm -f logs-*.tar.gz
